steps.message:
The change is a one-line edit, but it crosses a public interface boundary, so I'm stopping before touching it.

**The consequence:** `userId` in `GET /users` (`routes/users.js:6`) is a response field three consumers read — per `README.md`, the web app, the iOS app 3.2+, and the nightly partner export. Renaming it in place breaks all three at once, and the iOS clients can't be fixed by a deploy. The README also states the project's own rule: "Field names in the response are part of the contract; changes go through a versioned endpoint."

So the rename is exactly the kind of change the repo says shouldn't happen in place.

questions.question: Renaming userId breaks three live consumers of GET /users. How do you want to proceed?

options.label: Emit both fields
options.description: Return user_id alongside userId so new clients get the consistent name and existing consumers keep working. Drop userId later once the iOS app and partner export have migrated. No breakage, one line of duplication.

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: Add a v2 /users that returns user_id and leave the current endpoint as-is, matching the README's stated contract rule. Larger change: new route, wiring, and consumer migration plan.

options.label: Breaking rename anyway
options.description: Rename userId to user_id in place as originally asked. The web app, iOS 3.2+, and the nightly partner export will see the field disappear until each is updated.
